requirement_vague: Deleting a non-existent todo returns a failing response
requirement_precise: Register a user and login to get an access token. Call DELETE /todos/99999 (an ID that does not exist). Verify the response status code is 404 Not Found.
spec_evidence:
- Register a user and login. Create a todo with title 'Todo to Delete' and note the ID. Call DELETE /todos/{id}. Verify the response status is 200 OK. Then call GET /todos/{id} and verify the response is 404 Not Found (todo no longer exists).
- Register a user and login. Call PUT /todos/99999 with a valid todo body (id=99999, title='Test', isComplete=false). Verify the response status is 404 Not Found.
reasoning: The spec states that GET on a deleted todo returns 404 and that PUT on a non-existent todo returns 404, but it never states what DELETE should return when the target todo does not exist. Concluding that DELETE /todos/99999 must also return 404 would require extrapolation beyond the explicit text.
